The invention describes a computer system that includes a specially programmed server configured to perform media and web attribution functions. The server contains software modules designed to collect, process, analyze, and report information relating to media airings and web-based consumer activity. These modules work together to determine the relationship between media exposure and resulting web-originated transactions, such as online orders.

In operation, the server periodically obtains media data over a computer network from multiple media data source systems. The media data may include information identifying when and where particular media airings occurred, such as television, radio, streaming, or other advertising placements. This information can include airing times, channels or stations, geographic markets, campaign identifiers, creative identifiers, and other data useful for matching media events to later web activity.

The server also periodically obtains web tracking transaction data. This transaction data includes metrics associated with web-originated activities, including web orders, visits, conversions, form submissions, or other online events. For example, the data may identify the time of a web order, the product or service ordered, the originating website or landing page, geographic or device-related information, and other tracking parameters that help characterize the transaction.

Using the collected media data and web tracking transaction data, the system attributes each web order record in the transaction data to a particular media airing. This attribution may be performed by comparing the timing and characteristics of a web order with the timing and attributes of prior media airings. Based on programmed attribution rules, the server identifies the media airing most likely associated with the web order and records that association for reporting and analysis.

The system further provides a web attribution report that can be displayed to a user. The report is capable of being updated in real time, or near real time, as new media data and web tracking transaction data are received and processed. The report may present attributed web orders by media airing, campaign, channel, market, time period, or other relevant dimensions, thereby allowing users to evaluate the effectiveness of media placements in driving online activity.
outputs.L4:
A computer-implemented media attribution system is configured to determine how broadcast, streamed, or otherwise distributed media airings influence web-originated customer activity, including online orders. The system includes a programmed server, one or more data storage devices, and software modules that collect, process, correlate, and report data relating to media placements and web transactions.

In operation, the programmed server periodically receives or retrieves media airing data from one or more media data sources. The media airing data may include information identifying when and where a particular advertisement, program segment, promotional message, or other creative was aired or otherwise delivered. For example, the media airing data may identify a media channel, station, network, market, platform, airing time, duration, campaign, advertiser, product, and creative identifier. Each airing may therefore be associated with a specific creative and with contextual information describing the circumstances of the airing.

The server also periodically collects web tracking transaction data from one or more web tracking systems, e-commerce platforms, analytics systems, order management systems, or similar sources. The web tracking transaction data may include information relating to visits, clicks, sessions, leads, shopping cart activity, conversions, and completed web orders. For each web-originated order, the collected data may include a timestamp, order identifier, customer or session identifier, referring source, landing page, product ordered, order value, geographic information, device information, or other tracking attributes.

After collecting the media airing data and the web tracking transaction data, the programmed server processes the data to associate web activity and web orders with one or more media airings. The attribution process may compare the timing of a web transaction with the timing of media airings and determine whether the transaction occurred within a defined attribution window following a particular airing. The system may also use additional factors, such as geographic market, channel, creative identifier, campaign, product, customer location, or other matching criteria, to determine which airing or airings are most likely to have contributed to the web-originated order.

When a web order is attributed to a media airing, the system stores attribution information linking the order to the corresponding airing and to the creative associated with that airing. In some implementations, the system may assign the order to a single media airing. In other implementations, the system may allocate credit among multiple airings according to predetermined rules, weighting models, time-decay models, or other attribution logic. The attribution data may be updated as new media airing data and new web transaction data are received.

The system generates a web attribution report based on the processed attribution data. The report may identify, for each creative, campaign, media outlet, market, time period, or individual airing, the number of web visits, leads, orders, revenue, conversion rate, cost per order, return on advertising spend, or other performance metrics attributed to the airing or group of airings. The report may be accessible through a web-based interface, dashboard, exported file, application programming interface, or other reporting mechanism.

Because the server periodically collects and processes updated airing and transaction data, the web attribution report can be refreshed in real time or near real time. As additional media airings occur and additional web orders are placed, the system updates the attribution results and presents current performance information to advertisers, agencies, media planners, or other users. This enables users to measure the effectiveness of particular media airings and creatives in driving web-originated orders, compare performance across media channels and campaigns, and adjust media buying or creative strategy based on observed response data.

In some embodiments, a system, method, or device may be configured to perform one or more functions in a flexible and adaptable manner. The phrase “in some embodiments” is commonly used in technical and patent-related writing to describe optional features, variations, or implementations without limiting the scope of the overall concept.

For example, in some embodiments, a device may include a processor, a memory, and a communication interface. In some embodiments, the processor may execute instructions stored in the memory to analyze data, generate outputs, or control connected components. In some embodiments, the communication interface may enable the device to exchange information with remote servers, user devices, or other networked systems.

Using the phrase “in some embodiments” allows the description to cover multiple possible versions of an invention or design. It indicates that a feature may be present in certain implementations, but is not necessarily required in every implementation. This wording provides flexibility and helps explain how different configurations may achieve similar results.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style “in some embodiments” description for a computer system that attributes web orders to media airings using media data and web tracking transaction data, and generates a real-time web attribution report.
counterfactuals.output:
In some embodiments, a computer system is configured to attribute web orders to media airings using media data and web tracking transaction data, and to generate a real-time web attribution report. The computer system may include one or more processors, memory storing executable instructions, and one or more network interfaces configured to receive data from media data sources, web analytics systems, order processing systems, tag management systems, customer relationship management systems, or combinations thereof.

In some embodiments, the computer system receives media data representing a plurality of media airings. The media data may include, for each media airing, one or more of: a media asset identifier, campaign identifier, creative identifier, channel identifier, network identifier, station identifier, publisher identifier, geographic market identifier, airing start time, airing end time, scheduled airing time, actual airing time, program identifier, daypart, cost, impression estimate, audience demographic information, and media placement metadata. The media data may be received in real time, near real time, or in batch form from one or more broadcast monitoring systems, media buying platforms, ad servers, connected television platforms, radio monitoring systems, linear television systems, streaming media systems, or other media measurement sources.

In some embodiments, the computer system receives web tracking transaction data representing web sessions, web visits, cart events, conversion events, purchase events, lead submissions, subscriptions, or other user interactions with a website, mobile application, or other network-accessible property. The web tracking transaction data may include, for each transaction or event, one or more of: a timestamp, transaction identifier, order identifier, session identifier, visitor identifier, cookie identifier, device identifier, IP address, user agent, landing page, referring URL, UTM parameter, product identifier, cart value, order value, customer identifier, geographic location, conversion type, and event sequence data.

In some embodiments, the computer system normalizes the media data and the web tracking transaction data to a common time reference. For example, airing timestamps and web transaction timestamps may be converted to a common time zone, adjusted for latency, synchronized to a common clock, or mapped to discrete time intervals. In some embodiments, the system further normalizes campaign identifiers, creative identifiers, geographic market identifiers, and channel identifiers to enable comparison between heterogeneous media sources and web tracking sources.

In some embodiments, the computer system determines one or more attribution windows associated with respective media airings. An attribution window may define a time period beginning at, before, or after a media airing and ending after a predetermined duration. In some embodiments, the attribution window is selected based on media type, creative, product category, channel, time of day, historical response curve, geographic market, or other campaign parameter. For example, a first attribution window may be used for a television airing, a second attribution window may be used for a radio airing, and a third attribution window may be used for a streaming video impression.

In some embodiments, the computer system identifies web orders occurring within an attribution window associated with a media airing. The system may compare a web order timestamp with an airing timestamp and determine whether the web order falls within a response interval for the airing. In some embodiments, the system further compares geographic data associated with the web order to geographic data associated with the media airing. For example, the system may determine whether an IP-derived region, shipping address region, billing address region, designated market area, postal code, or other location attribute corresponds to a market in which the media airing occurred.

In some embodiments, the computer system attributes a web order to a media airing based on one or more attribution rules. The attribution rules may include, without limitation, a last-airing rule, first-airing rule, nearest-airing rule, weighted attribution rule, fractional attribution rule, decay-based attribution rule, market-matched attribution rule, creative-matched attribution rule, channel-priority rule, or probabilistic attribution rule. In some embodiments, if multiple media airings are candidates for attribution, the computer system assigns the web order to a selected airing based on temporal proximity, media cost, impression level, predicted response, historical conversion rate, geographic overlap, campaign priority, or a weighting function.

In some embodiments, the computer system computes an attribution score for each candidate pairing of a web order and a media airing. The attribution score may be based on a time difference between the airing and the order, a geographic match score, a campaign match score, a creative match score, an expected response curve, media spend, audience size, device characteristics, traffic source characteristics, or combinations thereof. The computer system may attribute the order to the media airing having the highest attribution score, or may allocate portions of the order value among multiple media airings according to respective attribution scores.

In some embodiments, the computer system distinguishes direct, organic, paid search, paid social, email, referral, and media-driven web orders. For example, the system may exclude orders associated with a direct digital advertising click, apply reduced weighting to orders associated with paid search, or classify orders as media-influenced when the order occurs within a media response interval and satisfies one or more additional criteria. In some embodiments, the system removes or adjusts for baseline web traffic by calculating an expected order volume absent a media airing and attributing only incremental orders above the baseline to one or more media airings.

In some embodiments, the computer system generates real-time attribution metrics based on the attributed web orders. The attribution metrics may include one or more of: attributed order count, attributed revenue, cost per order, cost per acquisition, return on ad spend, conversion rate, response rate, average order value, incremental revenue, media efficiency, attributed visits, attributed carts, attributed leads, attributed subscriptions, and confidence score. The metrics may be calculated at one or more levels of aggregation, including by airing, creative, campaign, channel, network, station, geographic market, program, daypart, product, or time interval.

In some embodiments, the computer system generates a real-time web attribution report. The report may include a user interface, dashboard, data table, chart, notification, downloadable file, application programming interface response, or machine-readable data feed. The report may present attributed web orders and associated media airings, including timestamps, campaign identifiers, order values, attribution scores, attribution windows, and calculated performance metrics. In some embodiments, the report is updated continuously or periodically as new media data and web tracking transaction data are received.

In some embodiments, the computer system streams media airing events and web transaction events into an event processing pipeline. The event processing pipeline may include a message queue, stream processor, rules engine, attribution engine, and reporting database. The stream processor may match web orders to candidate media airings in near real time and update the reporting database with attribution results. In some embodiments, the real-time web attribution report is refreshed within seconds or minutes after receipt of a web order or media airing event.

In some embodiments, the computer system stores attribution results in an attribution datastore. The attribution datastore may store records that associate an order identifier with a media airing identifier, an attribution score, an attributed revenue amount, an attribution rule identifier, a time difference, a geographic match indicator, and one or more audit fields. In some embodiments, the attribution datastore maintains historical attribution records to support trend analysis, campaign optimization, forecasting, and model training.

In some embodiments, the computer system provides filtering and drill-down functionality within the real-time web attribution report. A user may filter attribution results by date range, campaign, creative, channel, station, market, product, order status, attribution rule, attribution confidence, or other criteria. In some embodiments, selecting a reported metric causes the system to display underlying attributed orders, candidate media airings, excluded orders, baseline adjustments, or attribution calculations.

In some embodiments, the computer system generates alerts based on real-time attribution performance. For example, the system may transmit an alert when attributed orders exceed a threshold, cost per order falls below a threshold, return on ad spend exceeds a threshold, a media airing fails to generate an expected response, or a particular creative produces anomalous web activity. The alert may be provided through email, text message, dashboard notification, webhook, or another communication channel.

In some embodiments, the computer system uses historical media and web transaction data to adapt attribution parameters. For example, the system may determine response curves, baseline traffic levels, expected conversion rates, or optimal attribution windows for different media channels, creatives, programs, products, or markets. In some embodiments, a machine learning model is trained to predict a likelihood that a web order was influenced by a media airing, and the predicted likelihood is used as an attribution score or weighting factor.

In some embodiments, privacy-preserving techniques are applied to the web tracking transaction data. For example, visitor identifiers may be hashed, tokenized, truncated, aggregated, or otherwise anonymized before attribution processing. In some embodiments, attribution is performed using session-level, market-level, or aggregate event-level data without storing personally identifiable information.

In some embodiments, the computer system exposes an application programming interface through which a client device can request the real-time web attribution report. In response to a request specifying one or more report parameters, the system retrieves attribution results from the attribution datastore, aggregates the results according to the report parameters, and returns a report object including attributed order metrics and media performance metrics.

In some embodiments, the computer system is further configured to optimize media allocation based on the real-time web attribution report. For example, the system may identify media placements having high attributed revenue or low cost per order and generate recommendations to increase spending, decrease spending, change airing schedules, replace creatives, or modify campaign targeting. In some embodiments, the system automatically transmits optimization instructions to a media buying platform or campaign management system.

In some embodiments, a method performed by the computer system includes receiving media data identifying a plurality of media airings; receiving web tracking transaction data identifying a plurality of web orders; normalizing timestamps associated with the media airings and web orders; determining candidate media airings for respective web orders based on attribution windows; applying attribution rules to associate at least one web order with at least one media airing; calculating attribution metrics based on the association; and generating, in real time, a web attribution report presenting the attribution metrics.

In some embodiments, a non-transitory computer-readable medium stores instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform operations including ingesting media airing data and web tracking transaction data, matching web orders to media airings using temporal and contextual attribution criteria, calculating one or more attribution scores, storing attribution records, and providing a real-time report indicating media-driven web order performance.

counterfactuals.output:
A computer-implemented system for media attribution, comprising at least one programmed server communicatively coupled to one or more media monitoring data sources and one or more electronic transaction data sources. The programmed server is configured to receive media airing data corresponding to television or radio advertisement airings, the media airing data including at least an advertisement identifier and a time of airing. The programmed server is further configured to receive web transaction data corresponding to online orders, the web transaction data including at least transaction timing information and order information.

The programmed server stores the received media airing data and web transaction data in one or more databases and executes attribution logic to associate respective online orders with respective advertisement airings. The attribution logic may compare a time of an online order with one or more candidate advertisement airings, apply one or more attribution windows or rules, and determine a particular television or radio advertisement airing that caused, contributed to, or is otherwise attributable to the online order.

In response to determining an attribution between an online order and a media airing, the programmed server generates attribution information identifying the associated advertisement airing and the corresponding online order. The programmed server further provides, through a user interface, application programming interface, dashboard, alert, report, or data feed, substantially real-time attribution reporting indicating performance of the television or radio advertisement airings with respect to resulting online transactions.

In one embodiment, a method comprises: receiving, by a programmed server, media airing data associated with a plurality of television or radio advertisement airings; receiving, by the programmed server, web transaction data associated with a plurality of online orders; processing, by the programmed server, the media airing data and the web transaction data to identify temporal relationships between advertisement airings and online orders; determining, by the programmed server, for each of at least some of the online orders, a corresponding advertisement airing to which the online order is attributed; and outputting, by the programmed server in real time or near real time, attribution data that identifies the online orders and the advertisement airings to which the online orders are attributed.

In certain implementations, the attribution determination includes applying one or more configurable rules including an attribution time window following an advertisement airing, a priority rule among multiple candidate airings, a geographic market rule, a channel or station rule, an advertisement creative rule, a product or offer rule, or a weighting rule. The programmed server may update attribution results continuously as additional media airing data or web transaction data is received.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a legal/patent embodiment for an invention involving network-based collection of creative airing data and web-originated order tracking data, where a server attributes orders to media placements.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a computerized attribution system is provided for correlating broadcast or streaming media placements with web-originated transaction activity. The system includes at least one server communicatively coupled to one or more media scheduling data sources, one or more creative asset repositories, and one or more web order processing systems over a network.

The server is configured to receive creative airing data associated with one or more media placements. The creative airing data may include, without limitation, a creative identifier, campaign identifier, advertiser identifier, media outlet identifier, geographic market identifier, airing date, airing time, program identifier, placement duration, cost, audience estimate, and/or a broadcast, cable, satellite, connected television, streaming audio, streaming video, or other media distribution channel identifier. In certain implementations, the creative airing data is received from a traffic system, a media buying platform, a station log, an automated content recognition system, a set-top-box reporting system, a streaming ad server, or a third-party verification service.

The server is further configured to receive web-originated order tracking data from an order tracking system associated with an advertiser, merchant, or service provider. The web-originated order tracking data may include, for example, an order identifier, session identifier, cookie identifier, device identifier, user account identifier, landing page identifier, referrer identifier, promotional code, SKU or product identifier, order value, order timestamp, order status, shipping region, billing region, IP-derived location, and/or other transaction metadata. The order tracking data may be received through an application programming interface, pixel tag, server-to-server postback, batch file transfer, event stream, or database synchronization process.

In operation, the server stores the creative airing data and the web-originated order tracking data in one or more databases and normalizes the respective data sets into a common attribution format. Normalization may include converting timestamps to a common time zone, mapping media outlets to designated market areas, associating creative identifiers with campaign identifiers, deduplicating repeated order events, filtering canceled or fraudulent orders, and classifying order events by product, geography, customer type, or campaign objective.

The server applies an attribution engine to determine whether one or more web-originated orders are attributable to one or more media placements. In one embodiment, the attribution engine identifies candidate orders occurring within a predetermined attribution window following an airing of a creative asset. The attribution window may be defined by the advertiser, campaign, creative, media outlet, product type, daypart, geographic region, or other parameter. For example, orders received within thirty minutes, two hours, twenty-four hours, or another configurable period after a media placement may be evaluated as potentially attributable to that placement.

The attribution engine may compare the airing data and order tracking data using one or more matching criteria. The matching criteria may include temporal proximity between an airing timestamp and an order timestamp, geographic correspondence between a media market and an order location, use of a placement-specific uniform resource locator, use of a promotional code associated with the creative, traffic volume changes to a web property following the airing, product correspondence between the creative content and the ordered item, or other campaign-specific signals. In certain embodiments, the attribution engine applies a weighted scoring model in which each matching criterion contributes to an attribution score. If the attribution score exceeds a threshold, the server attributes the order, in whole or in part, to the media placement.

In another embodiment, the server performs fractional attribution where a single order may be attributed among multiple candidate media placements. The fractional allocation may be based on relative attribution scores, recency, reach, frequency, estimated audience, media spend, geographic overlap, or a decay function. For example, a more recent airing of the same creative in the same geographic market may receive a larger portion of the attribution credit than an earlier airing in a different market.

In still another embodiment, the server determines a baseline order rate for a product, advertiser, or campaign and identifies incremental orders associated with one or more media placements by comparing observed order volume during a post-airing response interval to the baseline order rate. The baseline may be determined using historical order data, non-airing periods, control markets, day-of-week patterns, seasonality, web traffic trends, or predictive modeling. The server may then attribute only the incremental portion of order activity to the media placement.

The server may generate attribution records, each attribution record associating at least one order or incremental order count with at least one media placement. Each attribution record may include a media placement identifier, creative identifier, order identifier or aggregated order count, attributed revenue, attribution score, attribution percentage, attribution window, geographic market, timestamp, and confidence value. The attribution records may be stored in a database and made available through a reporting interface, dashboard, API, or downloadable file.

In certain embodiments, the server calculates one or more performance metrics for the media placement or campaign, including cost per attributed order, cost per incremental order, attributed revenue, return on advertising spend, conversion rate, response curve, lift percentage, market-level performance, creative-level performance, daypart performance, media outlet performance, or frequency-adjusted performance. The server may display the performance metrics to a user and may enable the user to adjust media buying decisions, campaign budgets, creative rotations, or attribution parameters based on the calculated metrics.

In one implementation, the server receives a first data feed identifying that a particular creative was aired on a television station in a first designated market area at a first time. The server also receives, from an e-commerce server, order tracking events indicating that a plurality of orders were placed through a website after the first time. The server determines that at least a subset of the orders originated from locations within or associated with the first designated market area and occurred within a defined response interval following the airing. The server then generates attribution records attributing the subset of orders, or an incremental portion thereof, to the television airing of the creative.

In another implementation, the creative includes a web call-to-action, such as a vanity URL, QR code, promotional code, or campaign-specific landing page. The server maps the call-to-action to a corresponding creative identifier and media placement identifier. When an order tracking event includes the corresponding URL, code, or landing page identifier, the server uses the mapping as a deterministic attribution signal and may attribute the order to the associated creative airing, subject to deduplication and validation rules.

The system may include a privacy-preserving data handling module configured to hash, tokenize, truncate, aggregate, or otherwise protect personally identifiable information prior to storage or attribution processing. The server may perform attribution using pseudonymous identifiers or aggregated geographic and temporal data without requiring disclosure of personally identifiable customer information to media vendors.

The foregoing embodiment may be implemented using one or more processors executing instructions stored on one or more non-transitory computer-readable media. The instructions, when executed, cause the one or more processors to receive creative airing data, receive web-originated order tracking data, normalize and correlate the data, determine attribution of orders to media placements according to temporal, geographic, deterministic, probabilistic, or statistical attribution rules, and generate attribution records and campaign performance metrics based on the determined attribution.

in certain embodiments, the system calculates incremental response by comparing observed orders after an airing to an expected baseline derived from historical order patterns, seasonality, traffic trends, product availability, price changes, concurrent promotions, non-media marketing activity, weather, events, market controls, or machine-learning forecasts, and allocates revenue, conversions, return on ad spend, cost per acquisition, lift, conversion rate, response curve, saturation level, frequency effect, and confidence metrics to the corresponding airing records; the system may include a dashboard server and graphical user interface configured to display real-time attribution analytics including live airing timelines, order spikes, attributed revenue, incremental conversions, channel and creative performance, market-level heat maps, daypart comparisons, funnel metrics, confidence intervals, anomaly alerts, pacing indicators, spend efficiency, and drill-down views from campaign level to individual airing and individual order level subject to privacy controls, wherein the graphical user interface permits a user to filter by date range, campaign, media source, creative, market, program, product, customer segment, attribution model, or attribution window, and to export reports, trigger alerts, adjust media allocation recommendations, or automatically transmit optimized buy instructions to media planning or buying systems; and in still further embodiments, the system is implemented as a cloud-based, on-premises, or hybrid architecture using scalable storage and compute resources, APIs for bidirectional integration with advertising and commerce platforms, and configurable rules and machine-learning models that continuously refine attribution accuracy based on subsequent order outcomes, media delivery validation, and feedback from campaign performance, thereby enabling near real-time measurement of the relationship between advertising media airings and web orders and the display of actionable attribution analytics for optimizing advertising spend.
